context.objective: Document how we carry out Quarterly GP Workbook Production, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The procedure says the preparer confirms the approved start condition and scope, but does not specify the trigger. What event or notification actually initiates Quarterly GP Workbook Production?

The trigger is the fund team telling us that the main fund workbook for the same period is final and has been approved by the client. They give us the approved source totals and confirm that we may start. Until that happens we do not begin GP production. How often it comes round depends on the engagement: it can be quarterly, semiannual, annual or annual-only.
How do you verify and record the client's approval before beginning GP production?

As the preparer I check the fund workbook the fund team sent for the exact period, that it is the final version, that the client approval is there, and the GP investor totals. I keep the approved input version, the approval record and a production checklist, and a reviewer looks over that check. If the workbook is not final and client-approved for the same period I stop: no allocating, no posting and no output until the fund team and client give us the approved source. I do not know where the approval record is officially meant to be filed or how long we keep it. That has not been settled, and Operations, Records Management or Accounting Policy would have to confirm it.
Once you can start, how do you reconcile the beginning balances and carried-forward amounts?

I copy the controlled previous-period GP workbook and update the period. Then I tie the beginning balances and the carry we had already recorded back to the accounting records and to the prior approved deliverables. It has to agree with zero unexplained difference, and I keep that opening-balance reconciliation so the reviewer can check it. If the opening balances or the previously recorded carry do not reconcile, I stop. The reviewer and Accounting decide how the difference is resolved, and the workbook is not ready for production until it is.
Once the opening balances reconcile, what do you do next in the GP workbook?

Next I look for changes and tie the GP totals to the fund workbook. I go through the governing documents first and then the Activities and Tax Activities tabs to spot anything that changed. For each changed term I record the previous and current values, the effective date and the source, and I independently recalculate the affected results. The tabs only flag possible changes, they do not decide the treatment. Then I map every GP category to the fund workbook and confirm the amounts agree exactly. If a change is unsupported or conflicting I stop that calculation and we get a current interpretation from the governing document, the client or the adviser. After that I confirm the allocation method, the included records and the schedules with the client and lock that input set.
Once you lock that input set, how do you use it to produce the GP workbook results?

First I run the capital allocation using whichever method the client approved: across the full population, by deal or by tranche. I identify the records for realized events and reconcile the member allocations to the GP capital total. Then I calculate carry from inception through the current period for each component and schedule, combine the results and subtract the carry already recorded. That difference is the current-period entry. We never calculate carry for the current period on its own. A Controller reviews the calculation and the journal entry support, and that review has to be complete before the entry is posted. Once it is posted I update the workbook from the posted records and reconcile the entry, the workbook and the source. I do not know who is formally meant to post the entry or who has the authority to approve it before posting. Nobody has been named, and Process Governance and Accounting Operations would need to confirm that. After posting, the Controller reviews the completed workbook, with a Director if needed, every comment gets resolved and the final version is locked. Only then do we produce and release the client outputs.
Which role is accountable for the overall GP workbook production result?
